findings.evidence:
This commit changes timezone-sensitive paths to use `EvalContext.Location()` (StmtCtx TypeCtx) instead of `SessionVars.Location()`:
- `pkg/expression/helper.go:68` now converts `CURRENT_TIMESTAMP` via `ctx.Location()`.
- `pkg/table/column.go:636` now converts TIMESTAMP default values via `ctx.GetEvalCtx().Location()`.
`EvalContext.Location()` is derived from `StmtCtx.TypeCtx()` (`pkg/expression/contextimpl/sessionctx.go:196`, `pkg/expression/contextimpl/sessionctx.go:210`).
However, `SET_VAR` hints apply by calling `sessVars.SetSystemVarWithOldValAsRet` (`pkg/planner/optimize.go:190`) and for `time_zone` the sysvar setter only updates `SessionVars.TimeZone` (`pkg/sessionctx/variable/sysvar.go:1574`), without updating `StmtCtx` timezone (`pkg/sessionctx/stmtctx/stmtctx.go:497`). This allows `SessionVars.Location()` to differ from `EvalContext.Location()` within the same statement when `SET_VAR(time_zone=...)` is used, changing behavior vs first-parent for the touched paths.
findings.fix: When applying `SET_VAR` hints, refresh statement timezone after `time_zone` is set (e.g. in `pkg/planner/optimize.go` after `SetSystemVarWithOldValAsRet`, if `name == "time_zone"` then call `sessVars.StmtCtx.SetTimeZone(sessVars.Location())`). More robust: define a small “stmtctx refresh” hook for any sysvar that affects `StmtCtx.TypeCtx()` (timezone, type-flags related vars) and invoke it after hint application.
findings.impact: SQL statements using `/*+ SET_VAR(time_zone=...) */` can observe `@@time_zone` changed for the statement, but `CURRENT_TIMESTAMP`-derived values (e.g. `ON UPDATE CURRENT_TIMESTAMP` for `DATETIME`, and TIMESTAMP default-timezone conversions in `pkg/table/column.go`) may be computed using the *pre-hint* timezone (StmtCtx) instead of the hinted timezone. This is a correctness/compatibility regression relative to the first parent for the specific code paths changed in this commit, and can lead to wrong stored `DATETIME` values under time_zone hints.
findings.later_fix_evidence: Checked `remotes/upstream/master` (as of this workspace): `pkg/sessionctx/variable/sysvar.go` `time_zone` SetSession still only sets `s.TimeZone` (no `StmtCtx.SetTimeZone`), and `pkg/planner/optimize.go` set-var-hint loop still does not refresh `StmtCtx` timezone after applying `SetVars`.
findings.verify:
Add a regression test that exercises the changed paths under `SET_VAR(time_zone=...)`:
- Use a `DATETIME ... ON UPDATE CURRENT_TIMESTAMP` column (so the stored value depends on timezone), set a deterministic `@@timestamp`, run an `UPDATE /*+ SET_VAR(time_zone='+12:00') */ ...` and assert the updated `DATETIME` matches the +12:00 interpretation.
- Also add a unit-level assertion in planner: after applying `StmtHints.SetVars`, `sessVars.Location()` equals `sessVars.StmtCtx.TimeZone()` when `time_zone` is among the hinted vars.
findings.what: `SET_VAR(time_zone=...)` can diverge `SessionVars.TimeZone` from `EvalContext.Location()` (StmtCtx TypeCtx) during a statement; this commit moves some timezone-sensitive behavior (CURRENT_TIMESTAMP generation + TIMESTAMP default conversions) to use `EvalContext.Location()`, so those behaviors may ignore the hinted `time_zone` within the statement.

subject: expression: `BuildContext` read location from `EvalContext` instead of `SessionVars` (#52451)
summary: Review of `da0de56204b5908afc69949d78525ceea0512928` (PR #52451, first-parent diff). Main behavior change is switching some timezone reads from `SessionVars.Location()` to `EvalContext.Location()` (StmtCtx TypeCtx) in expression/table helpers; this can introduce a correctness regression for statements using `SET_VAR(time_zone=...)` because the hint updates `SessionVars.TimeZone` but does not refresh `StmtCtx` timezone, and upstream/master still appears to have the same mismatch.
